However, the ETS is considered a highly complex process (Lloret, Plaza, & Aker, 2018). The ETS is seen as an immersed task of ATS which employ different criteria to evaluate summaries. In general, the ETS has evaluated summaries under two main criteria: extrinsic and intrinsic (Jones & Galliers, 1995).

However, each metric evaluates summaries under different evaluation criteria. Based on this fact, several content metrics have been combined via ROSE and linear regression to improve the performance of automatic evaluation (Conroy and Dang, 2008, Ellouze et al., 2016).

The Summary Evaluation Environment (SEE) has been known as the first manual evaluation method to compare the candidate summary content against a set of human references (Lin and Hovy, 2002, Overet al., 2007). These metrics assess different aspects of the model’s ability to generate human-like, meaningful, and contextually accurate text.

Fluency: Fluency evaluates how natural and grammatically correct the generated text is. A fluent text follows the conventions of the target language, making it easy for humans to read and understand. Coherence: Coherence assesses how well the text holds together logically and thematically. Coherent text flows smoothly and maintains consistency in terms of ideas and context. Relevance: Relevance refers to how closely the generated text aligns with the input prompt or the task at hand.
